chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ibn Jabala, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the person in iḥrām who is shaded while he is in iḥrām. He said: 'No, except for a sick person, or one who has an ailment, or the one who cannot endure the sun.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: A person in the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or ʿUmrah

ai.seo_question: When is it permissible for a person in iḥrām to shade themselves from the sun?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isṭibṣār clarifies the exception to the general prohibition of shading the head while in iḥrām, permitting it specifically for those suffering from illness or an inability to endure the sun's heat. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of removing hardship (rafʿ al-ḥaraj), distinguishing between mere discomfort and genuine medical necessity or weakness.
